blocks.prompt: 2 (i) Using the Second Derivative Test, find local extreme values of \(f(x) = 8 - 2x^{2}\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh Second Derivative Test ka seedha sa sawal hai; sawal khud test ka naam le raha hai.
Diya: \(f(x) = 8 - 2x^{2}\). Find: local extreme values.
Rule: \(f'(c) = 0\) wale point par \(f''(c) < 0\) to maximum, \(f''(c) > 0\) to minimum.
Plan: \(f'\), \(f' = 0\), \(f''\), aur aakhir mein \(f\) ki value.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = 8 - 2x^{2}\).
Maloom karna: local extreme values.
Tareeqa: Second Derivative Test (2.10.4).

Stationary point
\[f'(x) = -4x = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0\]
Kyun: yeh test sirf un points par lagta hai jahan \(f'(c) = 0\) ho, is liye pehle yeh point dhoonda.

Second derivative
\[f''(x) = -4\]
\[f''(0) = -4 < 0\]
Kyun: \(f''\) negative hai, yani curve ulte pyale ki tarah hai: \(x = 0\) par relative maximum.

Value
\[f(0) = 8 - 0 = 8\]
Kyun: extreme value hamesha asal \(f\) se nikalti hai, \(f''\) se nahin.
Tasdeeq: \(f(\pm 1) = 6\), jo 8 se kam hai. Graph ulta parabola hai jis ki chotti \((0, 8)\) par hai.
blocks.final_answer: Local maximum value \(f(0) = 8\), \(x = 0\) par; koi local minimum nahin.

blocks.prompt: 2 (ii) Using the Second Derivative Test, find local extreme values of \(f(x) = x^{2} - x - 2\).
blocks.explanation:
Second Derivative Test ka sawal, ek quadratic function ke saath.
Diya: \(f(x) = x^{2} - x - 2\). Find: local extreme value.
Rule: \(f''\) ka sign.
Plan: \(f'(x) = 2x - 1 = 0\), phir \(f''\) se faisla, phir value.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = x^{2} - x - 2\).
Maloom karna: local extreme values.
Tareeqa: Second Derivative Test.

Stationary point
\[f'(x) = 2x - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{1}{2}\]
Kyun: power rule se derivative, phir seedhi (linear) equation hal ki.

Second derivative
\[f''(x) = 2 > 0\]
Kyun: \(f''\) positive hai (har jagah), yani seedha pyala: \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) par relative minimum.

Value
\[f\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right) = \tfrac{1}{4} - \tfrac{1}{2} - 2 = -\tfrac{9}{4}\]
Kyun: denominator 4 bana kar: \(\frac{1 - 2 - 8}{4} = -\frac{9}{4}\).
Dhyan dein: \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2} = \frac{1}{4}\), \(\frac{1}{2}\) nahin.
Tasdeeq: square complete karein: \(x^{2} - x - 2 = \left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right)^{2} - \frac{9}{4}\). Square kabhi negative nahin, is liye function \(-\frac{9}{4}\) se neeche nahin jata.
blocks.final_answer: Local minimum value \(f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = -\frac{9}{4}\), \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) par; koi local maximum nahin.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iii) Using the Second Derivative Test, find local extreme values of \(f(x) = x^{4} - 8x^{2} + 2\).
blocks.explanation:
Second Derivative Test ka sawal, jis mein teen stationary points niklenge.
Diya: \(f(x) = x^{4} - 8x^{2} + 2\). Find: local extreme values.
Rule: har stationary point par \(f''\) ka sign.
Plan: \(f'\) ko factorise kar ke teeno points, \(f''\), har point ka test, phir values.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = x^{4} - 8x^{2} + 2\).
Maloom karna: local extreme values.
Tareeqa: Second Derivative Test.

Stationary points
\[f'(x) = 4x^{3} - 16x\]
\[= 4x(x - 2)(x + 2) = 0\]
\[x = 0,\ x = 2,\ x = -2\]
Kyun: pehle \(4x\) common nikala, phir \(x^{2} - 4 = (x - 2)(x + 2)\) (squares ka farq).
Dhyan dein: \(4x\) ko divide kar ke phenk dena ghalti hai; us se \(x = 0\) wala point gum ho jata hai.

Second derivative
\[f''(x) = 12x^{2} - 16\]
\[f''(0) = -16 < 0 \text{ (maximum)}\]
\[f''(\pm 2) = 48 - 16 = 32 > 0 \text{ (minimum)}\]
Kyun: \(f''\) ka sign faisla karta hai: minus yani maximum, plus yani minimum.

Values
\[f(0) = 2\]
\[f(\pm 2) = 16 - 32 + 2 = -14\]
Kyun: values asal \(f\) mein rakh kar.
Tasdeeq: \(f\) even function hai (\(f(-x) = f(x)\)), yani graph \(y\)-axis ke dono taraf aaina hai. Is liye dono minima ki value ek honi chahiye, aur hai: \(-14\). Graph "W" ki shakal ka hai.
blocks.final_answer: Local maximum value \(f(0) = 2\), \(x = 0\) par; local minimum value \(-14\), \(x = -2\) aur \(x = 2\) dono par.

blocks.prompt: 2 (iv) Using the Second Derivative Test, find local extreme values of \(f(x) = (x + 2)^{2}(x - 3)\).
blocks.explanation:
Second Derivative Test ka sawal, jahan function do brackets ka product hai.
Diya: \(f(x) = (x + 2)^{2}(x - 3)\). Find: local extreme values.
Rule: product rule se \(f'\), phir \(f''\) ka sign.
Plan: product rule ke baad common factor \((x + 2)\) nikaalna; poora expand karne se kaam lamba ho jata hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = (x + 2)^{2}(x - 3)\).
Maloom karna: local extreme values.
Tareeqa: Second Derivative Test; product rule \(f'\) ko factorised shakal mein de deta hai.

Pehla derivative
\[f'(x) = 2(x + 2)(x - 3) + (x + 2)^{2}\]
\[= (x + 2)\left[2(x - 3) + (x + 2)\right]\]
\[= (x + 2)(3x - 4)\]
Kyun: product rule \((uv)' = u'v + uv'\), jahan \(u = (x + 2)^{2}\) (chain rule se \(u' = 2(x + 2)\)) aur \(v = x - 3\). Phir dono terms se \((x + 2)\) bahar nikala: bracket ke andar \(2x - 6 + x + 2 = 3x - 4\).

Stationary points
\[x = -2 \quad \text{or} \quad x = \dfrac{4}{3}\]
Kyun: har factor ko zero rakha.

Doosra derivative
\[f'(x) = 3x^{2} + 2x - 8\]
\[f''(x) = 6x + 2\]
\[f''(-2) = -10 < 0,\quad f''\left(\tfrac{4}{3}\right) = 10 > 0\]
Kyun: \(f''\) nikaalne ke liye \(f'\) ko expand karna aasaan hai: \((x + 2)(3x - 4) = 3x^{2} + 2x - 8\). \(-2\) par maximum, \(\frac{4}{3}\) par minimum.

Values
\[f(-2) = 0^{2}(-5) = 0\]
\[f\left(\tfrac{4}{3}\right) = \left(\tfrac{10}{3}\right)^{2}\left(-\tfrac{5}{3}\right) = -\tfrac{500}{27}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{4}{3} + 2 = \frac{10}{3}\) aur \(\frac{4}{3} - 3 = -\frac{5}{3}\); phir \(\frac{100}{9} \times \left(-\frac{5}{3}\right) = -\frac{500}{27}\).
Tasdeeq: \(-\frac{500}{27} \approx -18.52\). Qareeb ke points \(f(1) = 9(-2) = -18\) aur \(f(2) = 16(-1) = -16\) dono is se oonche hain, jaisa minimum ke paas hona chahiye.
blocks.final_answer: Local maximum value \(f(-2) = 0\), \(x = -2\) par; local minimum value \(f\left(\frac{4}{3}\right) = -\frac{500}{27}\), \(x = \frac{4}{3}\) par.

blocks.prompt: 2 (v) Using the Second Derivative Test, find local extreme values of \(f(x) = (x^{2} - 2x)e^{x}\).
blocks.explanation:
Second Derivative Test ka sawal, jis mein \(e^{x}\) ka factor hai.
Diya: \(f(x) = (x^{2} - 2x)e^{x}\). Find: local extreme values.
Rule: \(e^{x}\) kabhi zero nahin hota (hamesha positive), is liye equation mein sirf bracket ko zero karna hai.
Plan: product rule, \(e^{x}\) common, \(f' = 0\) hal, phir dobara product rule se \(f''\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(f(x) = (x^{2} - 2x)e^{x}\).
Maloom karna: local extreme values.
Tareeqa: Second Derivative Test; \(e^{x} > 0\) wali baat se hisaab chhota ho jata hai.

Pehla derivative
\[f'(x) = (2x - 2)e^{x} + (x^{2} - 2x)e^{x}\]
\[= e^{x}(x^{2} - 2)\]
Kyun: product rule; \(e^{x}\) ka derivative \(e^{x}\) hi hai. Bracket mein \(2x - 2 + x^{2} - 2x = x^{2} - 2\): \(2x\) aur \(-2x\) cancel ho gaye.

Stationary points
\[x^{2} - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = \pm\sqrt{2}\]
Kyun: \(e^{x}\) zero nahin ho sakta, is liye sirf \(x^{2} - 2 = 0\).

Doosra derivative
\[f''(x) = 2x e^{x} + (x^{2} - 2)e^{x}\]
\[= e^{x}(x^{2} + 2x - 2)\]
Kyun: \(e^{x}(x^{2} - 2)\) par dobara product rule.

\(x = \sqrt{2}\) ka test
\[f''(\sqrt{2}) = e^{\sqrt{2}}(2 + 2\sqrt{2} - 2)\]
\[= 2\sqrt{2}\,e^{\sqrt{2}} > 0\]
\[f(\sqrt{2}) = (2 - 2\sqrt{2})e^{\sqrt{2}}\]
Kyun: \(f'' > 0\), yani relative minimum. Value: \((\sqrt{2})^{2} - 2\sqrt{2} = 2 - 2\sqrt{2}\), aur \(f(\sqrt{2}) \approx -3.408\).
Tasdeeq: \(f(0) = 0\) aur \(f(2) = 0\); in ke darmiyan function negative hai aur \(x = \sqrt{2} \approx 1.414\) par lagbhag \(-3.408\) tak jata hai. Minimum wahi hai.
blocks.final_answer: Local maximum value \(f(-\sqrt{2}) = (2 + 2\sqrt{2})e^{-\sqrt{2}} \approx 1.174\), \(x = -\sqrt{2}\) par; local minimum value \(f(\sqrt{2}) = (2 - 2\sqrt{2})e^{\sqrt{2}} \approx -3.408\), \(x = \sqrt{2}\) par.
